clue.text: Nuts stimulated, it's up and finally inserted

indicators.note: something stimulated is stirred up, so the following letters are stirred into a new order
finally points to the very end of the next word, keeping only its closing letter

blocks.note: the letters of the phrase, taken as written before being mixed
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A smutty picture of arousal: something is up and finally goes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like the subject of a rude sentence, but it is the definition: STUPI from the mixed letters of IT'S UP, then D.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling an idea nuts dismisses it as crazy or foolish, a loose informal synonym for brainless.

clue.text: Civilians cynically taken out (claret drunk with Lola)

definitions.note: a description of the thing rather than a synonym; the answer is the adjective in 'collateral damage'

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and jumbled, so the named letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A satirical jab at military spin, with a boozy aside about Lola and her claret.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a jaundiced gloss on the military euphemism 'collateral damage', meaning civilians killed incidentally.
explanation.definitionFit: Military spokesmen describe incidental civilian deaths as collateral damage, a euphemism the clue sneers at.

clue.text: "Quite a knock, to live without corgis, somehow"

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified manner, so the dog word's letters are arranged in some other way
without is used in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: to be is to live or exist
the letters of corgis, rearranged

explanation.surface: A dig at the royals: a real blow would be living without corgis.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman's innings is a 'knock', so a big innings is quite a knock. Corgis are the Queen's famous dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket slang calls an innings a knock, and a large run total from one batsman makes a substantial one.

clue.text: see 24dn.
Eye clutched by Clegg's ultimate female enthusiast

indicators.note: something clutched is held inside, so one piece sits within the others
ultimate means last, so only the final letter of the politician's name is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of Clegg
Private Eye refers to itself as us, the magazine speaking
her is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: Private Eye is cuddled by Nick Clegg's last female admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue appears in Private Eye, so 'Eye' means the magazine itself: we, us. Nick Clegg was Lib Dem leader and deputy prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who pours out effusive, excessive praise is informally called this, much like an oil well spouting.

clue.text: Hurd, upbraided, holding tongue

indicators.note: the opening words hold the answer inside them, so read straight across their letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the boundary between the two words

explanation.surface: Douglas Hurd is scolded and keeps his mouth shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding tongue' suggests keeping quiet; tongue is really the definition, meaning language. Douglas Hurd was a Conservative foreign secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue is an old word for a language, and this is the official language of Pakistan.

clue.text: Penis Boy's fancy white top formal wear

the top of a word is its first letter, keeping just that one

the letters of boy, rearranged
the first letter of white

explanation.surface: A schoolboy-smutty image of a lad's fancy white dress shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: A dicky bow is British slang for a bow tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow tie is worn with a dinner jacket at black-tie events, so it counts as formal attire.

clue.text: Unacceptably more conservative than the Conservatives? Most certainly

definitions.text: Unacceptably more conservative than the Conservatives

blocks.clueFragment: Unacceptably more conservative than the Conservatives
blocks.note: first meaning: excessively right-wing
second meaning: an emphatic exclamation of agreement

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the phrase means overly right-wing; as a British and Australian exclamation it means 'absolutely'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial exclamation of emphatic agreement, and literally describes politics beyond the right wing.

clue.text: Artist's screen placed in front of Hirst's 'Number Two'

indicators.note: number two points to the second letter in the artist's name that follows

blocks.note: a guard, like a fireguard, screens something off
the second letter of Hirst

explanation.walkthrough: 'Placed in front of' just orders the pieces. Damien Hirst is a British artist, which makes 'Number Two' look like a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Francesco Guardi was an eighteenth-century Venetian painter famous for his views of the city.

clue.text: Shag retreat, a large marine presence

blocks.note: both are vulgar slang for having sex
to back is to move backwards, retreat

explanation.surface: A coy sexual encounter followed by a hasty withdrawal from a big presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine presence' looks like soldiers, but it means something present in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The humpback is a species of whale, a very big creature living in the ocean.

clue.text: Pain in the arse top bankers make them

blocks.note: first meaning: haemorrhoids
second meaning: large heaps of money, as in making a fortune

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pain in the arse' reads as an insult aimed at the bankers, but it is literal. The second definition is the idiom 'make piles' for getting rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Haemorrhoids are a painful rectal condition, and great heaps of cash are what wealthy financiers accumulate.

clue.text: Hardy gets to shag with new leader – feel bad about that

definitions.note: the answer is a retort, 'too bad', so the definition is a loose paraphrase

a coarser word for the same act

explanation.surface: Someone called Hardy gets to sleep with a new boss and should feel guilty about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The four-letter swear word has its F replaced by L. 'Hardy' looks like a name but is just an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The retort is said unsympathetically to someone complaining, meaning it is unfortunate but nothing can be done.

clue.text: City backing for Heath before switch of central characters in revolt

explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle two letters of RIOT swap, giving ROIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is the large Michigan city famous as the heart of the American motor industry.

clue.text: Kate endlessly dealt with manipulation, being addressed pompously

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Being lectured without any chance to reply is the idiom for one-way, condescending speech aimed at a listener.

clue.text: Jaunty bust rub alarm

blocks.note: pert means lively and cheeky
the letters of rub, rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like a bosom to match 'jaunty', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To alarm someone is to unsettle or disturb them, making the two verbs close synonyms.

clue.text: Scary utterance: "Hague, try blending with Left" – Tory leader

taken as written

the first letter of Tory

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tory leader' looks like a description of Hague, who led the Conservatives, but only gives its first letter.

clue.text: Dodgy, insecure lav wall – a great opportunity for prying by the authorities!

taken as written

clue.text: "Sod Jersey!" sort of bottle?

a jersey is a knitted top

explanation.surface: Someone curses the island of Jersey.

clue.text: Hard exterior of Conservative authority taking a criminal charge

taken as written

clue.text: Return of disease about genital area (amphetamines rejected)

clue.text: (& 4dn.) "Python gets the bird" rumour

clue.text: Local outing for those on benders?
